== Biography ==
Andrew Glasgow was born on 24 October 1746 and was baptised two days later, on 26 October, in Kilwinning, Ayrshire, Scotland. The parish transcript records the family's residence as Town, Kilwinning.<ref name="FMP">"Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564-1929," transcript, Findmypast ([https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3628386&tab=this record SCOT/OPR/BAP/3628386] : accessed 4 September 2026), Andrew Glasgow, born 24 Oct and baptised 26 Oct 1746, Kilwinning, son of John Glasgow and Mary Auld; residence Town, Kilwinning; citing OPR 599/2, item 2, p. 83.</ref> He was the son of [[Glasgow-2467|John Glasgow]] and [[Auld-1724|Mary Auld]].<ref name="FMP" />

The baptism is also indexed in the Kilwinning church registers held by ScotlandsPeople.<ref>Kilwinning parish baptism record for Andrew Glasgow, 26 Oct 1746, ScotlandsPeople, church registers, parish 599, reference 20/93.</ref>

=== Current evidence assessment ===

The parish transcript gives separate birth and baptism dates. Andrew's birth
was 24 October 1746; 26 October 1746 is his baptism date.
Its stated register range of 1789–1819 conflicts with the indexed 1746 dates. The original parish-register image has not been inspected, so the range discrepancy remains open; the Findmypast transcript is derivative evidence.<ref name="FMP" /> The baptism place and family residence do not independently establish the exact birthplace.

=== Possible A. Glascow, 1794 arrival ===
A. Glascow from Glasgow is named with H. Jurriens from Riga and J. Mark from Königsbergen in a shipping-arrival report for 24 June 1794, under the Rotterdam dateline of 25 June.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1335425007/ Rotterdamse courant, 26 June 1794, p.2].</ref>

Only the initial A. is given. The list probably names a shipmaster, but it does not state a vessel, full forename, sex, family or personal origin. Glasgow is the departure port. P. L. Markwaarden in the following entry is a different person.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2468]]. Adult in 1794 with an Ayrshire locality; no maritime occupation, Rotterdam link, or identifying family context is recorded.
